artworks.title: Plate 2: Maddalena and Enrico, the Children of Pedro González (Petrus Gonsalvus)
artworks.medium: watercolor and gold paint on parchment
artworks.dimensions: page size (approximate): 14.3 x 18.4 cm (5 5/8 x 7 1/4 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Lessing J. Rosenwald
artworks.description: This painting depicts two children standing upright, wearing elaborate garments. They face slightly to the right and look off in that direction. The children appear to have pale skin, but their faces are both covered in short brown fur or hair. Their eyes, noses, and mouths are still visible. The taller child on the left wears an embellished pink gown with a ruffled lace collar, puffy white sleeves, a bejeweled neckline, and a large cross pendant with jewels hanging from it. This child appears to have long hair on their head that is braided to look like a tiara, and the top of their head is covered with colorful jewels. The shorter child on the right stands with their hand resting on a rock on the right edge of the painting. They wear a bright pink gown with a ruffled lace collar and embroidery down the front and on the shoulders. They wear a tall pink hat. The ground beneath these two children is a light brown color with some small rocks, and behind them is plain paper. These figures are encircled in a gold oval frame with Latin text above and below it.

The objects are positioned within an ellipse, outlined in light orange, in the center of the image with Roman numerals 'XXX' to the right outside the ellipse.

artworks.dimensions: page size (approximate): 14.3 x 18.4 cm (5 5/8 x 7 1/4 in.)

artworks.description: This image depicts a large oval with text surrounding it. The central oval is hand-drawn in golden-brown on aged cream-colored paper. At the top and bottom of the drawing, there are inscriptions in various handwritings and colors. The top inscription is a Latin phrase in red ink: "Deum time, et mandata eius observa, hoc enim est omnis homo. Ecc, 12". In red ink at the bottom is another Latin phrase: "Non est dignus nomine somniis, qui vel unum diem totum velit esse in voluptate. Cic." On the right side of the oval, there is a small Roman numeral "III". The drawing appears to be part of a collection or series, potentially for educational or illustrative purposes, given the ink usage and simplicity of the composition.
